# EchoGuard

A camera-free sitting / standing time tracker. Two ESP32-S3 boards exchange
Wi-Fi packets across the room, and the Channel State Information (CSI) of
those packets changes when you sit, stand, walk or leave. A local web app shows
how long you have been sitting and standing today, reminds you to stand up,
keeps a daily history, shows general health information about prolonged
sitting, and exports your data so you can share it with a health provider.
No camera and no microphone are used.

> **Disclaimer.** EchoGuard is a hackathon research prototype. It is **not a
> medical device** and is **not medically validated**. Sitting and standing are
> estimated from Wi-Fi signals and may be wrong. No accuracy claims are made:
> the only number shown is a within-calibration self-check, which is
> optimistic and is not validated accuracy.

## Quick start

```bash
make setup                                          # or, without internet: make setup-offline
make test
make dashboard ARGS="--serial /dev/cu.usbmodem2101" # live: receiver plugged into the Mac
make dashboard-sim SCENARIO=desk_day                # SYNTHETIC demo, no hardware
```

The app opens at http://127.0.0.1:8050/ (use `make app` as a shorter alias
for `make dashboard`). Then open **Calibrate** and run the calibration once
for your room (1 min 35 s, hands-free, see below). Until the room is
calibrated the app shows *Unknown - Not calibrated*.

Hardware: the current firmware uses **ESP-NOW** directly between the two
boards (no router, no internet). The transmitter runs on wall power across the
room; the receiver is plugged into the Mac and streams `CSI_DATA` lines over
USB at 921600 baud. **No reflash is needed for this version**: the
sitting/standing tracker is entirely on the Python / web side.

## The web app

Pages (top navigation):

* **Today**: the current state in large text (*Sitting*, *Standing*,
  *Moving*, *Away* or *Unknown* with the reason), confidence, the current
  streak (*Sitting for 23 min*), tiles for sitting / standing / moving today,
  upright total, stand hours versus goal, sit-to-stand transitions and the
  longest sitting bout, plus an hourly bar chart. A stand reminder banner
  appears after 30 min of continuous sitting (*Snooze 10 min*, optional
  desktop notification after you allow it, and a short beep). Reminder
  settings are at the bottom of the page.
* **History**: last 7 or 30 days as a chart and a table (sitting, standing,
  moving, upright, average and longest sitting bout, transitions, stand hours).
* **Health**: general, non-prescriptive information about prolonged sitting
  (WHO 2020 guidelines; Dunstan et al., Diabetes Care 2012) next to your own
  7-day averages. It is not medical advice.
* **Share**: what is collected, a date range, CSV / JSON downloads and a
  print-friendly summary for a health provider.
* **Calibrate**: the timed calibration with spoken instructions (below).
* **Sensor**: data source (serial port or `auto`, replay file, simulation,
  Stop), connection status (packets/s, RSSI, data quality, sensor
  configuration) and a live motion score chart.

"Upright" means standing + moving, like Apple Watch stand hours. A
**SYNTHETIC** banner is shown whenever the source is the simulator, and a
*Replay, not saved* note during replays; neither is ever written to your
history.

The UI is plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript served by Flask, with no CDN, no web
fonts and a strict Content-Security-Policy. **Security note:** the dashboard
has **no authentication**. It binds to `127.0.0.1` by default; `--host
0.0.0.0` prints a warning. Use it only on a trusted network.

## Calibration

The posture model is specific to your room and board placement, so calibrate
once after setting up (and again after moving the boards or furniture).
Start the live source, open **Calibrate**, enter a room name, press **Test
sound** (this also unlocks audio in the browser) and then **Start
calibration**. The run is hands-free: a beep and a spoken instruction mark
every phase, so you know when to come back in even from outside the room.

Default timeline (each recorded step includes 1 s that is discarded while
the analysis window clears):

| At | What to do | Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00 | Press Start, leave the room | 15 s |
| 0:15 | Empty room recorded (stay out) | 21 s |
| 0:36 | Come back in | 10 s |
| 0:46 | Walk back and forth between the boards (recorded) | 16 s |
| 1:02 | Stop walking and stand still | 5 s |
| 1:07 | Standing still recorded (where you normally stand) | 21 s |
| 1:28 | Walk to the chair and sit down | 5 s |
| 1:33 | Sitting recorded (your usual chair) | 21 s |
| 1:54 | Done - total 1 min 54 s | |

The time to leave (0-60 s), to come back (0-60 s), to change position (0-30 s)
and every step duration can be changed before starting; the schedule and the
total update live. During the run the page shows a big countdown, the current
instruction, what comes next and a progress bar. Afterwards it shows the data
quality of each step (with **Redo** for a failed step), warnings (for example
*sitting and standing look similar at this placement*), the sitting-vs-standing
self-check labelled *within-calibration check, optimistic*, and **Save**.
Saved calibrations live in `data/calibration/` and load automatically when
the same sensor configuration is seen again. You can load another one or
clear the active one.

The equivalent API: `POST /api/calibration/start` (`{"placement": "office",
"auto": true, "lead_in_s": 15, "grace_s": 10, "transition_s": 5}`), then `POST
/api/calibration/step/start`; poll `GET /api/calibration/state` (the
`session.timeline` holds the schedule, `session.phase` the countdown and cue);
`POST /api/calibration/save`.

## How detection works

1. **Motion gating.** Each 1 s window gets a motion score (variance and diff
   energy of the normalised, filtered subcarrier amplitudes relative to the
   empty-room noise). High scores mean *Moving*.
2. **Posture model.** When the person is still, the amplitude profile across
   the 52 subcarriers is compared with the reference profiles recorded during
   calibration (empty room, standing still, sitting) to decide *Away*,
   *Standing* or *Sitting*, with a probability.
3. **Hysteresis.** A new state must be confident (default 60%) and persist for
   a few seconds before it is accepted, so brief fidgeting does not flip the
   state. Short gaps in the data are bridged; long ones become *Unknown*.

Daily totals, bouts and stand hours are stored in `data/posture.sqlite3`
(live data only).

## Limitations

* Location dependent: the model only works for the room and board placement
  it was calibrated in. Recalibrate when the boards, the chair or large
  furniture move.
* A person sitting or standing still away from the line between the two
  boards may change the signal very little and can read as *Away*.
* Sitting and standing can look similar at some placements; the calibration
  warns when they do. Put the TX-RX line near the chair at seated torso height.
* One person at a time. Pets, fans and moving curtains add motion.
* The within-calibration self-check is optimistic (same session, same person)
  and is not validated accuracy.

## Data, privacy and export

Only time spent sitting, standing, moving and away, and reminder responses,
are stored, locally, in `data/posture.sqlite3`. No camera, no audio, and
nothing is sent anywhere automatically. **Share** (or
`GET /api/posture/export?format=csv|json&days=30`) downloads a file you can
give to a health provider; the print summary includes the method and the
disclaimer.

## Architecture
# EchoGuard sitting / standing tracker: developer commands (macOS / Linux).
#   make setup          create .venv and install pinned requirements (needs internet)
#   make setup-offline  recreate .venv from a Python that already has the deps (no network)
#   make setup-ml       optional: install scikit-learn/joblib for Random Forest training
#   make test           run the unit tests
#   make ports          list serial ports and likely ESP32 boards (read-only)
#   make monitor        print live CSI stats from the receiver (PORT=auto by default)
#   make dashboard      start the local web app on http://127.0.0.1:8050/ (ARGS="--serial /dev/cu.usbmodem2101")
#   make app            alias for make dashboard
#   make simulate       CLI monitor on SYNTHETIC simulated CSI (SCENARIO=demo, DURATION=0 = until Ctrl-C)
#   make dashboard-sim  web app on the SYNTHETIC simulation (SCENARIO=demo; desk_day for sitting/standing)
#   make evaluate       legacy: replay a recorded session through the fall heuristic (SESSION=data/recordings/<id>)
#   make train-rf       optional Random Forest training (needs make setup-ml)
#   make clean          remove caches (keeps .venv and data/)

VENV    := .venv
PY      := $(VENV)/bin/python
PORT    ?= auto
BAUD    ?= 921600
SCENARIO ?= demo
DURATION ?= 0
SESSION ?=
# Extra arguments for the dashboard, e.g. make dashboard ARGS="--serial auto"
ARGS    ?=

# Online setup: prefer Homebrew Python 3.11, then 3.12, then python3.11/3.12 on PATH.
# Python 3.14 is avoided on purpose (binary wheels for the pinned deps may be missing).
PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP ?= $(firstword $(wildcard /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11 /usr/local/bin/python3.11 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 $(HOME)/miniconda3/bin/python3.12) $(shell command -v python3.11 2>/dev/null) $(shell command -v python3.12 2>/dev/null))

# Offline setup: an interpreter that already has numpy/scipy/pandas/pyserial/flask/pytest.
# Uses PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP only when it was given explicitly (command line or environment).
ifneq ($(filter command line environment,$(origin PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP)),)
OFFLINE_PYTHON ?= $(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP)
else
OFFLINE_PYTHON ?= $(HOME)/miniconda3/bin/python3.12
endif

IMPORT_CHECK := import importlib.metadata as m, numpy, scipy, pandas, serial, flask, pytest; \
	print('deps OK:', ', '.join(p + ' ' + m.version(p) for p in ('numpy', 'scipy', 'pandas', 'pyserial', 'flask', 'pytest')))

.PHONY: setup setup-offline setup-ml test ports monitor dashboard app simulate dashboard-sim evaluate train-rf clean

setup:
	@if [ -z "$(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP)" ]; then echo "No python3.11/python3.12 found. Install with: brew install python@3.11"; exit 1; fi
	@echo "Using $(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP) ($$($(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP) --version))"
	@if [ ! -x "$(PY)" ]; then $(PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP) -m venv $(VENV); fi
	$(PY) -m pip install --upgrade pip
	$(PY) -m pip install -r requirements.txt
	$(PY) -c "$(IMPORT_CHECK)"

setup-offline:
	@if [ ! -x "$(OFFLINE_PYTHON)" ]; then echo "$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) not found. Pass one with: make setup-offline PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP=/path/to/python3"; exit 1; fi
	@echo "Using $(OFFLINE_PYTHON) ($$($(OFFLINE_PYTHON) --version)) with --system-site-packages (no network)"
	@$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) -c "$(IMPORT_CHECK)" || { echo "$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) lacks required packages (see requirements.txt)"; exit 1; }
	rm -rf $(VENV)
	$(OFFLINE_PYTHON) -m venv --system-site-packages $(VENV)
	$(PY) -c "$(IMPORT_CHECK)"

setup-ml:
	$(PY) -m pip install -r requirements-ml.txt

test:
	$(PY) -m pytest -q tests/

ports:
	$(PY) -m backend.cli ports

monitor:
	$(PY) -m backend.cli monitor --port $(PORT) --baud $(BAUD)

dashboard:
	$(PY) -m dashboard $(ARGS)

app: dashboard

# SYNTHETIC data, no ESP32 needed: make simulate SCENARIO=potential_fall DURATION=12
simulate:
	$(PY) -m backend.cli monitor --simulate $(SCENARIO) --duration $(DURATION)

dashboard-sim:
	$(PY) -m dashboard --simulate $(SCENARIO) $(ARGS)

# Heuristic check on recorded takes: make evaluate SESSION=data/recordings/<session_id>
evaluate:
	@if [ -z "$(SESSION)" ]; then echo "usage: make evaluate SESSION=data/recordings/<session_id>"; exit 2; fi
	$(PY) -m backend.cli evaluate --session $(SESSION)

# Optional (needs make setup-ml): Random Forest with session-held-out evaluation
train-rf:
	$(PY) -m backend.ml.train_rf --recordings data/recordings $(ARGS)

clean:
	rm -rf .pytest_cache
	find . -name __pycache__ -type d -prune -not -path "./$(VENV)/*" -exec rm -rf {} +

"""Streaming CSI signal processing and motion features.

Per packet (``SignalProcessor.process``):

1. take the valid subcarrier amplitudes (:func:`valid_subcarrier_amplitudes`;
   52 LLTF subcarriers on classic chips, NaN where masked; on C5/C6 columns
   that have never been non-zero, i.e. guard/null subcarriers, are dropped by
   masking them as NaN),
2. per-packet mean normalisation (``amp / mean(amp)``) to suppress AGC / gain
   jumps that scale all subcarriers together (the raw mean is kept as
   ``mean_amplitude``),
3. Hampel outlier rejection per subcarrier over the last ``hampel_window``
   packets (a value further than ``hampel_k`` scaled MADs from the median is
   replaced by the median),
4. EMA smoothing (``ema_alpha``).

Over a sliding window of ``window_s`` seconds (host timestamps) it computes:

* ``variance``: mean over subcarriers of the temporal std of the smoothed,
  normalised amplitude,
* ``diff_energy``: RMS of the first difference over time (temporal feature),
* ``baseline_deviation``: mean ``|profile - baseline_mean| / baseline_std``
  over subcarriers, using the calibration baseline when one is set, otherwise
  a slow adaptive EMA reference profile (``reference_tau_s``),
* ``motion_score``: ``0.5 * (variance / var_ref + diff_energy / diff_ref)``
  where the references are the calibrated empty-room noise levels (so an empty
  room scores about 1.0) or, uncalibrated, ``uncalibrated_*_ref`` defaults.

Frames (:class:`MotionFrame`) are emitted at ``frame_rate_hz`` of packet time,
not per packet. Each frame carries a data-quality verdict with reasons. Only
numpy is used so the module can be reused by offline training tools.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import time
import warnings
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np

from .config import ProcessingConfig
from .csi_parser import FAMILY_C5C6, CSIPacket, valid_subcarrier_amplitudes

#: Minimum std used when dividing by a baseline / reference std (normalised units).
STD_FLOOR = 1e-3
#: Minimum Hampel scale so a perfectly constant history does not flag tiny noise.
HAMPEL_FLOOR = 1e-3
#: MAD -> std for Gaussian data.
MAD_SCALE = 1.4826

# Quality reason codes (each reason string starts with one of these).
Q_NO_DATA = "no_data"
Q_LOW_RATE = "low_packet_rate"
Q_LOW_FILL = "low_window_fill"
Q_LAYOUT = "layout_changed"
Q_STALE = "stale"
Q_FEW_PACKETS = "insufficient_packets"


@dataclass
class Baseline:
    """Empty-room reference (set by calibration in Milestone 3)."""

    mean_profile: np.ndarray
    std_profile: np.ndarray
    noise_variance: Optional[float] = None
    noise_diff: Optional[float] = None
    name: str = ""


@dataclass
class MotionFrame:
    ts: float
    motion_score: Optional[float]
    variance: Optional[float]
    diff_energy: Optional[float]
    baseline_deviation: Optional[float]
    mean_amplitude: Optional[float]
    rssi: Optional[float]
    packet_rate: Optional[float]
    quality_ok: bool
    quality_reasons: list = field(default_factory=list)
    n_packets: int = 0
    window_fill: float = 0.0
    n_subcarriers: int = 0
    calibrated: bool = False
    baseline_source: str = "adaptive"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        d = asdict(self)
        for k, v in d.items():
            if isinstance(v, float) and not math.isfinite(v):
                d[k] = None
        return d


@dataclass
class _Entry:
    ts: float
    smoothed: np.ndarray
    mean_amp: float
    rssi: float


def _finite_or_none(x) -> Optional[float]:
    if x is None:
        return None
    x = float(x)
    return x if math.isfinite(x) else None


class SignalProcessor:
    """Streaming processor. Not thread-safe; feed it from a single thread."""

    def __init__(self, config: Optional[ProcessingConfig] = None) -> None:
        self.config = config or ProcessingConfig()
        self.baseline: Optional[Baseline] = None
        self.layout: Optional[tuple] = None
        self.layout_changes = 0
        self.invalid_packets = 0
        self.outliers_replaced = 0
        self.packets_processed = 0
        self.last_profile: Optional[np.ndarray] = None   # normalised, Hampel-filtered
        self.last_smoothed: Optional[np.ndarray] = None  # + EMA
        self.last_raw: Optional[np.ndarray] = None       # raw amplitudes (masked)
        self.last_frame: Optional[MotionFrame] = None
        self._layout_change_ts: Optional[float] = None
        self._last_frame_ts: Optional[float] = None
        self._reset_history()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- baseline
    def set_baseline(self, mean_profile, std_profile, noise_variance: Optional[float] = None,
                     noise_diff: Optional[float] = None, name: str = "") -> None:
        mean_profile = np.asarray(mean_profile, dtype=float)
        std_profile = np.asarray(std_profile, dtype=float)
        if mean_profile.shape != std_profile.shape or mean_profile.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError("baseline mean and std profiles must be 1-D arrays of equal length")
        self.baseline = Baseline(mean_profile, std_profile, noise_variance, noise_diff, name)

    def clear_baseline(self) -> None:
        self.baseline = None

    @property
    def baseline_active(self) -> bool:
        """True when a baseline is set and matches the current subcarrier layout."""
        b = self.baseline
        return b is not None and self.layout is not None and b.mean_profile.size == self.layout[1]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- state
    def _reset_history(self) -> None:
        self._hist: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self._hist_idx = 0
        self._ema: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self._ref_mean: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self._ref_var: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self._active: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self._window: deque = deque()
        self._start_ts: Optional[float] = None
        self._last_ts: Optional[float] = None

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Forget all history (keeps config and baseline)."""
        self._reset_history()
        self.layout = None
        self._layout_change_ts = None
        self._last_frame_ts = None
        self.last_profile = self.last_smoothed = self.last_raw = None
        self.last_frame = None

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- per packet
    def process(self, pkt: CSIPacket) -> Optional[MotionFrame]:
        """Consume one packet. Returns a :class:`MotionFrame` when one is due."""
        ts = float(pkt.host_ts) if pkt.host_ts is not None else time.time()
        amps = np.asarray(valid_subcarrier_amplitudes(pkt), dtype=float)
        layout = (pkt.chip_family, int(amps.size))

        if layout != self.layout:
            if self.layout is not None:
                self.layout_changes += 1
                self._layout_change_ts = ts
            self._reset_history()
            self.layout = layout
        elif self._last_ts is not None and ts < self._last_ts:
            # host time went backwards (e.g. a different replay): start over
            self._reset_history()
        if self._start_ts is None:
            self._start_ts = ts
        self._last_ts = ts

        if pkt.chip_family == FAMILY_C5C6:
            nonzero = np.nan_to_num(amps, nan=0.0) > 0
            self._active = nonzero if self._active is None else (self._active | nonzero)
            amps = np.where(self._active, amps, np.nan)

        finite = np.isfinite(amps)
        mean_amp = float(np.mean(amps[finite])) if finite.any() else float("nan")
        if not math.isfinite(mean_amp) or mean_amp <= 0:
            self.invalid_packets += 1
            return self._maybe_emit(ts)

        self.packets_processed += 1
        norm = amps / mean_amp
        filt = self._hampel(norm)
        smooth = self._smooth(filt)
        self._update_reference(smooth, ts)
        self.last_raw, self.last_profile, self.last_smoothed = amps, filt, smooth

        self._window.append(_Entry(ts, smooth, mean_amp, float(pkt.rssi)))
        cutoff = ts - self.config.window_s
        while self._window and self._window[0].ts < cutoff:
            self._window.popleft()
        return self._maybe_emit(ts)

    def _hampel(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        w = max(1, int(self.config.hampel_window))
        if self._hist is None:
            self._hist = np.full((w, x.size), np.nan)
            self._hist_idx = 0
        self._hist[self._hist_idx % w] = x
        self._hist_idx += 1
        if w < 3:
            return x.copy()
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            med = np.nanmedian(self._hist, axis=0)
            mad = np.nanmedian(np.abs(self._hist - med), axis=0)
        count = np.isfinite(self._hist).sum(axis=0)
        scale = np.maximum(MAD_SCALE * np.nan_to_num(mad, nan=0.0), HAMPEL_FLOOR)
        outlier = (count >= 3) & np.isfinite(x) & (np.abs(x - med) > self.config.hampel_k * scale)
        n_out = int(outlier.sum())
        if n_out:
            self.outliers_replaced += n_out
            return np.where(outlier, med, x)
        return x.copy()

    def _smooth(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        a = float(self.config.ema_alpha)
        if self._ema is None:
            self._ema = x.copy()
        else:
            prev = self._ema
            blended = np.where(np.isfinite(prev), a * x + (1.0 - a) * prev, x)
            self._ema = np.where(np.isfinite(x), blended, prev)
        return self._ema.copy()

    def _update_reference(self, x: np.ndarray, ts: float) -> None:
        if self._ref_mean is None:
            self._ref_mean = x.copy()
            self._ref_var = np.where(np.isfinite(x), 0.0, np.nan)
            self._ref_ts = ts
            return
        dt = max(0.0, ts - self._ref_ts)
        self._ref_ts = ts
        tau = max(1e-3, float(self.config.reference_tau_s))
        a = 1.0 - math.exp(-dt / tau) if dt > 0 else 1.0 / 1000.0
        fin = np.isfinite(x)
        init = fin & ~np.isfinite(self._ref_mean)
        upd = fin & ~init
        delta = np.where(upd, x - self._ref_mean, 0.0)
        self._ref_mean = np.where(init, x, self._ref_mean + a * delta)
        self._ref_var = np.where(init, 0.0, np.where(upd, (1.0 - a) * (self._ref_var + a * delta ** 2),
                                                     self._ref_var))

    def _maybe_emit(self, ts: float) -> Optional[MotionFrame]:
        period = 1.0 / self.config.frame_rate_hz if self.config.frame_rate_hz > 0 else 0.0
        if self._last_frame_ts is not None and ts - self._last_frame_ts < period and ts >= self._last_frame_ts:
            return None
        self._last_frame_ts = ts
        frame = self.compute_frame(ts)
        self.last_frame = frame
        return frame

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- features
    def compute_frame(self, now: Optional[float] = None) -> MotionFrame:
        """Features and quality over the window ending at ``now`` (host time;
        default: the newest packet). Values are ``None`` when not computable."""
        cfg = self.config
        calibrated = self.baseline_active
        source = "calibration" if calibrated else "adaptive"
        n_sc = self.layout[1] if self.layout else 0
        if not self._window:
            t = now if now is not None else (self._last_ts if self._last_ts is not None else time.time())
            return MotionFrame(t, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, False, [f"{Q_NO_DATA}: no valid CSI packets"],
                               n_subcarriers=n_sc, calibrated=calibrated, baseline_source=source)

        t_last = self._window[-1].ts
        now = t_last if now is None else float(now)
        reasons = []
        age = now - t_last
        if age > cfg.stale_after_s:
            reasons.append(f"{Q_STALE}: no packets for {age:.1f} s")

        lo = now - cfg.window_s
        wins = [e for e in self._window if lo <= e.ts <= now]
        n = len(wins)
        effective = min(cfg.window_s, now - self._start_ts) if self._start_ts is not None else 0.0
        rate = n / effective if effective > 0 else None
        fill = (wins[-1].ts - wins[0].ts) / cfg.window_s if n >= 2 and cfg.window_s > 0 else 0.0
        fill = min(1.0, fill)

        if rate is None or rate < cfg.min_packet_rate_hz:
            shown = "n/a" if rate is None else f"{rate:.1f} Hz"
            reasons.append(f"{Q_LOW_RATE}: {shown} < {cfg.min_packet_rate_hz:g} Hz")
        if fill < cfg.min_window_fill:
            reasons.append(f"{Q_LOW_FILL}: {fill:.2f} < {cfg.min_window_fill:g}")
        if self._layout_change_ts is not None and lo <= self._layout_change_ts <= now:
            reasons.append(f"{Q_LAYOUT}: CSI subcarrier layout changed in this window")

        variance = diff_energy = deviation = score = None
        mean_amp = rssi = None
        if n:
            mean_amp = float(np.mean([e.mean_amp for e in wins]))
            rssi = float(np.mean([e.rssi for e in wins]))
        if n >= 3:
            X = np.vstack([e.smoothed for e in wins])
            cols = np.isfinite(X).sum(axis=0) >= 2
            if cols.any():
                Xc = X[:, cols]
                with warnings.catch_warnings():
                    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
                    variance = _finite_or_none(np.nanmean(np.nanstd(Xc, axis=0)))
                    d = np.diff(Xc, axis=0)
                    diff_energy = _finite_or_none(np.sqrt(np.nanmean(d ** 2))) if np.isfinite(d).any() else None
                    profile = np.nanmean(X, axis=0)
                    deviation = self._deviation(profile, cols)
        else:
            reasons.append(f"{Q_FEW_PACKETS}: {n} packets in window")

        if variance is not None and diff_energy is not None:
            var_ref, diff_ref = cfg.uncalibrated_variance_ref, cfg.uncalibrated_diff_ref
            if calibrated:
                b = self.baseline
                if b.noise_variance and b.noise_variance > 0:
                    var_ref = b.noise_variance
                if b.noise_diff and b.noise_diff > 0:
                    diff_ref = b.noise_diff
            score = 0.5 * (variance / max(var_ref, 1e-12) + diff_energy / max(diff_ref, 1e-12))

        return MotionFrame(
            ts=now, motion_score=_finite_or_none(score), variance=variance, diff_energy=diff_energy,
            baseline_deviation=deviation, mean_amplitude=_finite_or_none(mean_amp), rssi=_finite_or_none(rssi),
            packet_rate=_finite_or_none(rate), quality_ok=not reasons, quality_reasons=reasons, n_packets=n,
            window_fill=float(fill), n_subcarriers=n_sc, calibrated=calibrated, baseline_source=source,
        )

    def _deviation(self, profile: np.ndarray, cols: np.ndarray) -> Optional[float]:
        if self.baseline_active:
            ref_mean = self.baseline.mean_profile
            ref_std = self.baseline.std_profile
        elif self._ref_mean is not None:
            ref_mean = self._ref_mean
            ref_std = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.nan_to_num(self._ref_var, nan=0.0), 0.0))
        else:
            return None
        ok = cols & np.isfinite(profile) & np.isfinite(ref_mean) & np.isfinite(ref_std)
        if not ok.any():
            return None
        z = np.abs(profile[ok] - ref_mean[ok]) / np.maximum(ref_std[ok], STD_FLOOR)
        return _finite_or_none(np.mean(z))

    def reference_profile(self) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        """Current adaptive reference profile (normalised amplitudes) or None."""
        return None if self._ref_mean is None else self._ref_mean.copy()

"""Guided self-calibration: noise levels, baseline profile and motion thresholds.

Workflow (:class:`CalibrationSession`), each step recorded for a fixed span of
packet time while the engine runs:

1. ``empty_baseline`` - empty, stationary room (15-30 s, default 20 s)
2. ``walking``        - a person walks across the sensing area (default 15 s)
3. ``standing_still`` - a person stands still where they normally stand (default 20 s)
4. ``sitting``        - seated on the chair they normally use (default 20 s)
5. compute            - :func:`compute_calibration`

A run (:meth:`CalibrationSession.begin`) waits ``lead_in_s`` (time to leave the
room, default 15 s), then records; with ``auto`` the remaining steps follow by
themselves, with ``grace_s`` between the empty room and walking (time to come
back in, default 10 s) and ``transition_s`` between consecutive steps with a
person (stop walking / sit down, default 5 s). :func:`build_timeline` gives the
planned schedule (with speakable cues) shown and read aloud by the dashboard;
with the defaults and a 1 s settle time a full run takes 114 s.

Frames come from the engine thread (``Engine.add_frame_hook``) together with
``SignalProcessor.last_smoothed`` (the normalised, filtered amplitude profile
that the features and the baseline deviation use). Nothing is driven by the UI
refresh.

Computed values:

* empty-room baseline: per-subcarrier mean and std of the smoothed profile,
* noise levels: median / p95 of variance, diff energy, baseline deviation and
  motion score in the empty room; ``noise_variance`` / ``noise_diff`` (medians)
  become the motion-score normalisation, so a calibrated empty room scores ~1,
* per-step distributions (median, quartiles, p5/p95) of the recomputed
  calibrated motion score and other features, and per-step mean profiles,
* preliminary thresholds from the empty/still p95 and the walking median/p95
  (monotonic ``low < movement < rapid``; falls back to conservative defaults
  with a warning when walking is not clearly separable from stillness),
* a sitting / standing / empty posture model (:mod:`backend.posture`) with a
  within-calibration self-check (optimistic, not a validated accuracy).

Calibrations are persisted as ``data/calibration/<sensor_key>.json``, where the
key combines placement, chip family, TX MAC, channel, secondary channel and
CSI length. Calibrations computed from synthetic (simulated) data carry
``synthetic: true`` and a ``__synthetic`` key suffix, and are never applied to
real sources automatically (and not manually either).

These thresholds are preliminary heuristics, not validated detection limits.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import math
import re
import threading
import time
import warnings
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np

from . import __version__
from . import posture
from .config import DATA_DIR, MotionThresholds
from .posture import json_list as _json_list
from .processing import STD_FLOOR
from .recording import iso, validate_placement, write_json_atomic

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_DIR = DATA_DIR / "calibration"
#: 2 adds ``posture_model``; format-1 files (no posture model) still load.
CALIBRATION_FORMAT = 2
KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,159}$")
SYNTHETIC_SUFFIX = "__synthetic"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StepSpec:
    key: str
    title: str
    instructions: str
    default_s: float
    min_s: float
    max_s: float
    cue: str = ""                   # short speakable prompt when the step begins (read aloud by the UI)
    person_present: bool = True     # False: the room must be empty during the step
    prepare: str = ""               # what to do during the transition before the step


STEPS = [
    StepSpec("empty_baseline", "Empty room baseline",
             "Leave the room and keep everything still: no people, pets, fans or moving curtains between "
             "or near the two boards.", 20.0, 15.0, 30.0,
             cue="Recording the empty room. Stay outside.", person_present=False),
    StepSpec("walking", "Walking",
             "Walk back and forth across the room at a normal pace, crossing the line between the two boards.",
             15.0, 5.0, 60.0, cue="Come in and walk back and forth between the two boards.",
             prepare="Walk to the area between the two boards"),
    StepSpec("standing_still", "Standing still",
             "Stand still at the spot where you normally stand, for example at your standing desk. Breathe "
             "normally and keep your arms still.", 20.0, 5.0, 60.0,
             cue="Stand still where you normally stand.", prepare="Stop walking and stand still"),
    StepSpec("sitting", "Sitting",
             "Sit in the chair you normally use, at the spot where you usually work, and stay seated as you "
             "normally would.", 20.0, 5.0, 60.0,
             cue="Sit in the chair you normally use and stay seated.", prepare="Sit down on your chair now"),
]
STEP_KEYS = [s.key for s in STEPS]
STEP_BY_KEY = {s.key: s for s in STEPS}

#: Wait before the first recorded step of a run (time to leave the room).
MAX_LEAD_IN_S = 60.0
#: Wait between an empty-room step and the next step with a person (time to
#: come back in).
MAX_GRACE_S = 60.0
#: Wait between two consecutive steps with a person (stop walking and stand
#: still / walk to the chair and sit down).
MAX_TRANSITION_S = 30.0
#: Defaults for a one-click run from the dashboard.
DEFAULT_LEAD_IN_S = 15.0
DEFAULT_GRACE_S = 10.0
DEFAULT_TRANSITION_S = 5.0
#: Spoken after the last step of a run.
DONE_CUE = "Calibration recording finished. You can get up now."


def _seconds(value, name: str, hi: float) -> float:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value) \
            or not (0 <= value <= hi):
        raise CalibrationError(f"{name} must be 0-{hi:g} s")
    return float(value)


def mmss(seconds: float) -> str:
    """``m:ss``-style offset with two-digit minutes, e.g. ``01:35``."""
    s = max(0, int(round(float(seconds))))
    return f"{s // 60:02d}:{s % 60:02d}"


def build_timeline(keys, durations: dict, lead_in_s: float = 0.0, grace_s: float = 0.0,
                   settle_s: float = 0.0, transition_s: float = 0.0) -> dict:
    """Planned wall-clock schedule for recording ``keys`` back to back.

    Phases, in order: an optional ``lead_in`` before the first step (time to
    leave the room), each ``step`` (``settle_s`` discarded while the analysis
    window clears, then the step duration), an optional ``grace`` period before
    a step with a person that follows an empty-room step (time to come back in)
    and an optional ``transition`` between two consecutive steps with a person
    (time to get into position). Each phase has ``kind``, ``key`` (the step it
    belongs to), ``title``, speakable ``cue``, human ``instruction``,
    ``start_s`` / ``end_s`` / ``length_s`` (seconds from pressing Start) and
    ``when`` / ``until`` (``mm:ss`` offsets).
    """
    phases = []
    t = 0.0

    def add(kind, key, title, cue, instruction, length):
        nonlocal t
        phases.append({"kind": kind, "key": key, "title": title, "cue": cue, "instruction": instruction,
                       "start_s": round(t, 3), "end_s": round(t + length, 3), "length_s": round(length, 3),
                       "when": mmss(t), "until": mmss(t + length)})
        t += length

    prev = None
    for i, key in enumerate(keys):
        spec = STEP_BY_KEY[key]
        dur = float(durations[key])
        if i == 0 and lead_in_s > 0:
            if not spec.person_present:
                add("lead_in", key, "Leave the room now",
                    f"Leave the room now. Recording the empty room starts in {lead_in_s:g} seconds.",
                    f"Leave the room within {lead_in_s:g} seconds of pressing Start and stay outside until "
                    "you hear 'Come back in'.", lead_in_s)
            else:
                add("lead_in", key, "Get ready",
                    f"Get ready. {spec.title} starts in {lead_in_s:g} seconds.",
                    f"{spec.prepare or 'Get into position'}. Recording starts {lead_in_s:g} seconds after "
                    "pressing Start.", lead_in_s)
        elif prev is not None and spec.person_present and not prev.person_present:
            if grace_s > 0:
                add("grace", key, "Come back in",
                    f"Come back in. {spec.title} starts in {grace_s:g} seconds.",
                    f"Come back into the room. You have {grace_s:g} seconds before {spec.title.lower()} "
                    "starts.", grace_s)
        elif prev is not None and spec.person_present and prev.person_present and transition_s > 0:
            prepare = spec.prepare or "Get into position"
            add("transition", key, "Get into position",
                f"{prepare}. Recording starts in {transition_s:g} seconds.",
                f"{prepare}. You have {transition_s:g} seconds before {spec.title.lower()} is recorded.",
                transition_s)
        add("step", key, spec.title, spec.cue,
            f"{spec.instructions} Recording takes {settle_s + dur:g} seconds.", settle_s + dur)
        prev = spec
    return {"phases": phases, "total_s": round(t, 3), "total": mmss(t), "settle_s": settle_s,
            "done_cue": DONE_CUE}


#: A step needs this fraction of frames with sufficient data quality ...
MIN_OK_FRACTION = 0.8
#: ... and at least this many good frames (or half the expected frames).
MIN_OK_FRAMES = 20
#: Walking median must exceed the quiet (empty/still) p95 by this factor.
SEPARATION_RATIO = 1.5
#: Minimum relative gaps enforced between thresholds.
MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW = 1.1
RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT = 1.2
#: Floor for the noise references (normalised amplitude units).
NOISE_FLOOR = 1e-6
FEATURES = ("motion_score", "variance", "diff_energy", "baseline_deviation")


class CalibrationError(ValueError):
    """Invalid request, state, or data that cannot be calibrated (HTTP 400)."""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def _slug_part(value) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"[^0-9a-z]", "", str(value).lower())
    return s or "na"


def sensor_part(sensor: Optional[dict], synthetic: bool = False) -> Optional[str]:
    """Placement-independent part of the calibration key (None if unknown)."""
    if not sensor or not sensor.get("chip_family"):
        return None
    sec = sensor.get("secondary_channel")
    part = (f"{_slug_part(sensor.get('chip_family'))}_{_slug_part(sensor.get('tx_mac') or 'unknown')}"
            f"_ch{_slug_part(sensor.get('channel'))}-{_slug_part(sec if sec is not None else 'na')}"
            f"_len{_slug_part(sensor.get('csi_len'))}")
    return part + (SYNTHETIC_SUFFIX if synthetic else "")


def sensor_key(sensor: dict, placement: str, synthetic: bool = False) -> str:
    """``<placement>__<chip>_<txmac>_ch<ch>-<sec>_len<len>[__synthetic]``."""
    part = sensor_part(sensor, synthetic)
    if part is None:
        raise CalibrationError("sensor configuration unknown (no CSI packets seen yet)")
    return f"{validate_placement(placement)}__{part}"


def validate_key(key) -> str:
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not KEY_RE.match(key):
        raise CalibrationError("invalid calibration key")
    return key


def _stats(values) -> Optional[dict]:
    a = np.asarray([v for v in values if v is not None], dtype=float)
    a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
    if a.size == 0:
        return None
    p = np.percentile(a, [5, 25, 50, 75, 95])
    return {"n": int(a.size), "min": float(a.min()), "p05": float(p[0]), "p25": float(p[1]), "median": float(p[2]),
            "p75": float(p[3]), "p95": float(p[4]), "max": float(a.max()), "mean": float(a.mean())}


def _profile_stats(profiles: list):
    if not profiles:
        return None, None
    P = np.vstack(profiles).astype(float)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        return np.nanmean(P, axis=0), np.nanstd(P, axis=0)


def _to_array(values) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([np.nan if v is None else v for v in values], dtype=float)


# -------------------------------------------------------------- step data
@dataclass
class StepData:
    key: str
    duration_s: float
    status: str = "pending"            # pending | recording | done | failed
    failure: Optional[str] = None
    settle_s: float = 0.0              # frames in the first settle_s are skipped (window still holds the previous step)
    t0: Optional[float] = None
    t0_hint: Optional[float] = None    # packet time the step starts at when chained directly to the previous one
    t_last: Optional[float] = None     # packet time of the last frame seen during the step
    wall_start: Optional[float] = None
    total: int = 0
    ok: int = 0
    reasons: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)
    features: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: {k: [] for k in FEATURES})
    profiles: list = field(default_factory=list)
    layout: Optional[tuple] = None
    sensor: Optional[dict] = None
    synthetic: Optional[bool] = None
    source_kind: Optional[str] = None
    problems: list = field(default_factory=list)
    last_quality: Optional[dict] = None

    @property
    def elapsed_s(self) -> float:
        if self.t0 is None or self.t_last is None:
            return 0.0
        return max(0.0, self.t_last - self.t0 - self.settle_s)

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        spec = STEP_BY_KEY[self.key]
        return {
            "key": self.key, "title": spec.title, "instructions": spec.instructions,
            "duration_s": self.duration_s, "status": self.status, "failure": self.failure,
            "elapsed_s": round(self.elapsed_s, 2), "frames": self.total, "ok_frames": self.ok,
            "ok_fraction": round(self.ok / self.total, 3) if self.total else None,
            "top_reasons": [{"reason": r, "count": c} for r, c in self.reasons.most_common(3)],
            "last_quality": self.last_quality,
        }


def step_problems(sd: StepData, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0) -> list:
    """Reasons why a step's data is insufficient (empty list = OK)."""
    problems = list(sd.problems)
    if sd.total == 0:
        return problems + ["no motion frames were received (is a data source running?)"]
    frac = sd.ok / sd.total
    min_ok = max(MIN_OK_FRAMES, int(0.5 * sd.duration_s * max(frame_rate_hz, 1.0)))
    top = ", ".join(f"{r} x{c}" for r, c in sd.reasons.most_common(3))
    if frac < MIN_OK_FRACTION:
        problems.append(f"only {frac:.0%} of frames had sufficient data quality (need {MIN_OK_FRACTION:.0%})"
                        + (f"; main reasons: {top}" if top else ""))
    if sd.ok < min_ok:
        problems.append(f"only {sd.ok} frames with sufficient quality (need at least {min_ok})")
    if sd.elapsed_s < 0.9 * sd.duration_s:
        problems.append(f"covered {sd.elapsed_s:.1f} s of {sd.duration_s:g} s")
    if sd.key == "empty_baseline" and len(sd.profiles) < min_ok:
        problems.append("not enough amplitude profiles for the baseline")
    return problems


# --------------------------------------------------------------- compute
def build_posture_model(steps: dict, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0):
    """``(model, None)`` or ``(None, reason)``: the sitting / standing / empty
    posture model from the recorded step profiles plus its self-check."""
    by_class = {cls: steps[key].profiles for key, cls in posture.STEP_CLASSES.items() if key in steps}
    try:
        model = posture.fit_posture_model(by_class, k=posture.DEFAULT_K)
    except ValueError as e:
        return None, str(e)
    model["self_check"] = posture.temporal_self_check(by_class, frame_rate_hz, k=posture.DEFAULT_K)
    model["note"] = ("Location-dependent reference profiles from one calibration run; the self-check is "
                     f"a {posture.SELF_CHECK_LABEL}. Not a medical measurement.")
    return model, None


def compute_calibration(steps: dict, placement: str, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0,
                        defaults: Optional[MotionThresholds] = None, now: Optional[float] = None) -> dict:
    """Derive baseline, noise levels and thresholds from recorded steps.

    ``steps`` maps step keys to :class:`StepData`. Raises
    :class:`CalibrationError` (with every reason) when a step is missing or its
    data quality was insufficient.
    """
    defaults = defaults or MotionThresholds()
    problems = []
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        sd = steps.get(key)
        if sd is None or sd.total == 0:
            problems.append(f"{STEP_BY_KEY[key].title}: not recorded")
            continue
        for p in step_problems(sd, frame_rate_hz):
            problems.append(f"{STEP_BY_KEY[key].title}: {p}")
    if problems:
        raise CalibrationError("cannot compute calibration: " + "; ".join(problems))

    empty = steps["empty_baseline"]
    layouts = {steps[k].layout for k in STEP_KEYS}
    if len(layouts) != 1:
        raise CalibrationError("cannot compute calibration: the CSI layout differs between steps")
    warnings_out = []

    ev = np.asarray(empty.features["variance"], dtype=float)
    ed = np.asarray(empty.features["diff_energy"], dtype=float)
    noise_variance = float(np.median(ev))
    noise_diff = float(np.median(ed))
    if noise_variance < NOISE_FLOOR or noise_diff < NOISE_FLOOR:
        warnings_out.append("empty-room noise is essentially zero; noise references were floored "
                            f"at {NOISE_FLOOR:g} (is the signal real and varying?)")
    noise_variance = max(noise_variance, NOISE_FLOOR)
    noise_diff = max(noise_diff, NOISE_FLOOR)

    base_mean, base_std = _profile_stats(empty.profiles)

    def deviation(profile):
        ok = np.isfinite(profile) & np.isfinite(base_mean) & np.isfinite(base_std)
        if not ok.any():
            return None
        return float(np.mean(np.abs(profile[ok] - base_mean[ok]) / np.maximum(base_std[ok], STD_FLOOR)))

    step_out = {}
    scores = {}
    for key in STEP_KEYS:
        sd = steps[key]
        v = np.asarray(sd.features["variance"], dtype=float)
        d = np.asarray(sd.features["diff_energy"], dtype=float)
        s = 0.5 * (v / noise_variance + d / noise_diff)
        scores[key] = s
        devs = [deviation(p) for p in sd.profiles]
        pm, ps = _profile_stats(sd.profiles)
        step_out[key] = {
            "title": STEP_BY_KEY[key].title,
            "duration_s": sd.duration_s,
            "elapsed_s": round(sd.elapsed_s, 2),
            "frames": sd.total,
            "ok_frames": sd.ok,
            "ok_fraction": round(sd.ok / sd.total, 3),
            "stats": {
                "motion_score": _stats(s.tolist()),
                "variance": _stats(sd.features["variance"]),
                "diff_energy": _stats(sd.features["diff_energy"]),
                "baseline_deviation": _stats(devs),
                "motion_score_uncalibrated": _stats(sd.features["motion_score"]),
            },
            "profile_mean": _json_list(pm) if pm is not None else [],
            "profile_std": _json_list(ps) if ps is not None else [],
        }

    q = lambda key, pct: float(np.percentile(scores[key], pct))  # noqa: E731
    quiet_p95 = max(q("empty_baseline", 95), q("standing_still", 95))
    walk_med = q("walking", 50)
    walk_p95 = q("walking", 95)
    separable = walk_med >= SEPARATION_RATIO * quiet_p95
    if separable:
        gap = walk_med - quiet_p95
        low = quiet_p95 + 0.25 * gap
        movement = quiet_p95 + 0.5 * gap
        rapid = max(1.5 * walk_p95, 2.0 * movement)
    else:
        warnings_out.append(
            f"walking is not clearly separable from the empty room / standing still (walking median "
            f"{walk_med:.2f} vs quiet p95 {quiet_p95:.2f}, need x{SEPARATION_RATIO:g}); using conservative "
            "default thresholds. Check the board placement and that the person crossed the line between "
            "the boards, then recalibrate.")
        low = max(defaults.low, 1.2 * quiet_p95)
        movement = max(defaults.movement, 1.5 * low)
        rapid = max(defaults.rapid, 2.0 * movement)
    if movement < MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW * low:
        movement = MOVEMENT_OVER_LOW * low
        warnings_out.append("movement threshold raised to keep it above the stillness threshold")
    if rapid < RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT * movement:
        rapid = RAPID_OVER_MOVEMENT * movement
        warnings_out.append("rapid threshold raised to keep it above the movement threshold")
    if q("sitting", 50) >= rapid:
        warnings_out.append("ordinary sitting scored above the rapid-movement threshold; rapid movement may be "
                            "flagged during normal sitting")

    posture_model, posture_error = build_posture_model(steps, frame_rate_hz)
    if posture_model is None:
        warnings_out.append(f"no sitting/standing posture model: {posture_error}")
    else:
        warnings_out.extend(posture.quality_warnings(posture_model))

    now = time.time() if now is None else now
    noise = {f: step_out["empty_baseline"]["stats"][f] for f in ("variance", "diff_energy", "baseline_deviation")}

"""Sitting vs standing posture model built from calibration amplitude profiles.

Pure numpy (no scikit-learn). The inputs are the smoothed, mean-normalised
amplitude profiles (``SignalProcessor.last_smoothed``, one per good motion
frame) recorded during the calibration steps ``sitting``, ``standing_still``
and ``empty_baseline``. A person sitting or standing at a fixed spot changes
the static multipath pattern, so the per-subcarrier profile shifts.

Model (:func:`fit_posture_model`): per class and per subcarrier the mean and
std (std floored at :data:`backend.processing.STD_FLOOR`), a Fisher score per
subcarrier between sitting and standing
(``|mu_sit - mu_stand| / sqrt(var_sit + var_stand)``) and the indices of the
``k`` most discriminative subcarriers. :func:`score_profile` evaluates a
diagonal Gaussian log-likelihood over the selected subcarriers (non-finite
entries are ignored), :func:`classify_profile` turns it into a label and
softmax probabilities.

:func:`temporal_self_check` trains on one half of each step and tests on the
other half (both ways) using 2 s block averages. It is a within-calibration
self-check: optimistic, not a validated accuracy. The model is a location
dependent heuristic reference, not a medical measurement.

Models are plain JSON-compatible dicts (lists, ``None`` for non-finite
values), so they can be stored in calibration files and reused by other
components without conversion.

:class:`PostureClassifier` applies a model live, per engine frame, with
hysteresis (states sitting / standing / moving / away / unknown); it never
reports sitting or standing without a model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import warnings
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable, Optional

import numpy as np

from .config import PostureConfig
from .processing import STD_FLOOR

MODEL_KIND = "diagonal-gaussian"
MODEL_FORMAT = 1
#: Posture classes, in display order.
CLASSES = ("sitting", "standing", "empty")
#: The two classes the subcarrier selection discriminates.
SIT_STAND = ("sitting", "standing")
#: Calibration step key -> posture class.
STEP_CLASSES = {"sitting": "sitting", "standing_still": "standing", "empty_baseline": "empty"}
DEFAULT_K = 16
SELF_CHECK_BLOCK_S = 2.0
SELF_CHECK_LABEL = "within-calibration self-check, optimistic, not a validated accuracy"
#: Warn below these values.
MIN_SELF_CHECK_ACCURACY = 0.8
MIN_FISHER = 1.0
SIMILAR_WARNING = ("sitting and standing look similar at this placement; move the boards so the line between "
                   "them passes near the chair at seated torso height, then recalibrate")
_LOG_2PI = math.log(2.0 * math.pi)


def json_list(arr) -> list:
    """Float list rounded to 6 decimals, ``None`` for non-finite values."""
    return [round(float(v), 6) if v is not None and math.isfinite(v) else None for v in np.asarray(arr, dtype=float)]


def _to_array(values) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([np.nan if v is None else v for v in values], dtype=float)


def _stack(profiles, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
    rows = [np.asarray(p, dtype=float).ravel() for p in profiles]
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError(f"no profiles for class '{name}'")
    widths = {r.size for r in rows}
    if len(widths) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"profiles of class '{name}' have different lengths")
    return np.vstack(rows)


def _ordered(classes: Iterable[str]) -> list:
    classes = list(classes)
    return [c for c in CLASSES if c in classes] + [c for c in classes if c not in CLASSES]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- fit
def fit_posture_model(profiles_by_class: dict, k: int = DEFAULT_K, std_floor: float = STD_FLOOR) -> dict:
    """Per-class diagonal Gaussian over the ``k`` subcarriers that best
    separate sitting from standing.

    ``profiles_by_class`` maps class names (``sitting`` and ``standing`` are
    required, ``empty`` optional) to sequences of 1-D profiles of equal length.
    Raises :class:`ValueError` for missing classes or inconsistent shapes.
    """
    if not isinstance(profiles_by_class, dict):
        raise ValueError("profiles_by_class must be a dict")
    for name in SIT_STAND:
        if len(profiles_by_class.get(name) or []) < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 profiles for class '{name}'")
    k = int(k)
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError("k must be at least 1")
    names = _ordered(n for n, p in profiles_by_class.items() if p is not None and len(p) > 0)
    means, stds, counts = {}, {}, {}
    width = None
    for name in names:
        P = _stack(profiles_by_class[name], name)
        if width is None:
            width = P.shape[1]
        elif P.shape[1] != width:
            raise ValueError("profiles of different classes have different lengths")
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            mu = np.nanmean(P, axis=0)
            sd = np.nanstd(P, axis=0)
        means[name] = mu
        stds[name] = np.maximum(sd, std_floor)       # NaN stays NaN
        counts[name] = int(P.shape[0])
    mu_s, mu_t = means["sitting"], means["standing"]
    var = stds["sitting"] ** 2 + stds["standing"] ** 2
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        fisher = np.abs(mu_s - mu_t) / np.sqrt(var)
    finite = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(fisher))
    order = finite[np.argsort(-fisher[finite], kind="stable")]
    selected = [int(i) for i in order[:k]]
    return {
        "kind": MODEL_KIND,
        "format": MODEL_FORMAT,
        "classes": names,
        "n_subcarriers": int(width),
        "means": {n: json_list(means[n]) for n in names},
        "stds": {n: json_list(stds[n]) for n in names},
        "counts": counts,
        "fisher": json_list(fisher),
        "selected": selected,
        "k": len(selected),
        "best_fisher": round(float(fisher[selected[0]]), 6) if selected else None,
        "std_floor": std_floor,
    }


def validate_model(model) -> dict:
    """Check the structure of a (possibly loaded) model; returns it or raises ValueError."""
    if not isinstance(model, dict) or model.get("kind") != MODEL_KIND:
        raise ValueError("not a posture model")
    try:
        width = int(model["n_subcarriers"])
        classes = list(model["classes"])
        selected = [int(i) for i in model["selected"]]
        for c in classes:
            if len(model["means"][c]) != width or len(model["stds"][c]) != width:
                raise ValueError(f"class '{c}' has the wrong number of subcarriers")
    except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
        raise ValueError(f"posture model is incomplete: {e}") from None
    if not all(c in classes for c in SIT_STAND):
        raise ValueError("posture model needs the sitting and standing classes")
    if not selected or any(not (0 <= i < width) for i in selected):
        raise ValueError("posture model has invalid subcarrier indices")
    return model


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- score
def score_profile(model: dict, profile, classes: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None) -> dict:
    """Diagonal Gaussian log-likelihood per class over the selected subcarriers.

    Only subcarriers that are finite in the profile and in every scored class
    are used, so the values are comparable between classes. Returns ``{}``
    when no selected subcarrier is usable. Raises :class:`ValueError` when the
    profile length differs from the model.
    """
    if profile is None:
        x = np.array([])
    elif isinstance(profile, np.ndarray):
        x = profile.astype(float).ravel()
    else:
        x = _to_array(list(profile))
    width = int(model["n_subcarriers"])
    if x.size != width:
        raise ValueError(f"profile has {x.size} subcarriers, the posture model expects {width}")
    names = list(model["classes"]) if classes is None else [c for c in classes if c in model["classes"]]
    if not names:
        return {}
    idx = np.asarray(model["selected"], dtype=int)
    xs = x[idx]
    mus = {c: _to_array(model["means"][c])[idx] for c in names}
    sds = {c: _to_array(model["stds"][c])[idx] for c in names}
    mask = np.isfinite(xs)
    for c in names:
        mask &= np.isfinite(mus[c]) & np.isfinite(sds[c]) & (sds[c] > 0)
    if not mask.any():
        return {}
    out = {}
    for c in names:
        z = (xs[mask] - mus[c][mask]) / sds[c][mask]
        out[c] = float(np.sum(-0.5 * z * z - np.log(sds[c][mask]) - 0.5 * _LOG_2PI))
    return out


def classify_profile(model: dict, profile, classes: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None):
    """``(label, {class: probability})`` via a softmax of the log-likelihoods;
    ``(None, {})`` when the profile has no usable selected subcarrier."""
    ll = score_profile(model, profile, classes)
    if not ll:
        return None, {}
    names = list(ll)
    v = np.array([ll[c] for c in names], dtype=float)
    p = np.exp(v - v.max())
    p /= p.sum()
    probs = {c: float(pi) for c, pi in zip(names, p)}
    return max(probs, key=probs.get), probs


# -------------------------------------------------------------- self-check
def block_average(profiles, block_n: int) -> list:
    """NaN-safe means of consecutive blocks of ``block_n`` profiles (full blocks
    only; all profiles as one block when there are fewer than ``block_n``)."""
    rows = list(profiles)
    if not rows:
        return []
    block_n = max(1, int(block_n))
    chunks = [rows[i:i + block_n] for i in range(0, len(rows) - block_n + 1, block_n)] or [rows]
    out = []
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
        for chunk in chunks:
            out.append(np.nanmean(np.vstack([np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in chunk]), axis=0))
    return out


def _tally(results: dict) -> dict:
    per = {}
    tot = cor = 0
    for c, (n, ok) in results.items():
        per[c] = {"blocks": n, "correct": ok, "accuracy": round(ok / n, 4) if n else None}
        tot += n
        cor += ok
    return {"per_class": per, "accuracy": round(cor / tot, 4) if tot else None, "blocks": tot}


def temporal_self_check(profiles_by_class: dict, frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0, k: int = DEFAULT_K,
                        block_s: float = SELF_CHECK_BLOCK_S, std_floor: float = STD_FLOOR) -> dict:
    """Temporal split: fit on the first half of each class, test 2 s block
    averages of the second half, and vice versa.

    Returns accuracy per class and overall for all classes, and for the
    sitting-vs-standing decision alone (``sit_stand``). Labelled as a
    within-calibration self-check (optimistic, not a validated accuracy).
    """
    block_n = max(1, int(round(float(frame_rate_hz) * float(block_s))))
    out = {"label": SELF_CHECK_LABEL,
           "method": f"temporal split (first half / second half of each step, both ways), "
                     f"{block_s:g} s block averages",
           "block_s": block_s, "block_frames": block_n, "available": False, "reason": None}
    names = _ordered(n for n, p in profiles_by_class.items() if p is not None and len(p) > 0)
    halves = {}
    for n in names:
        rows = list(profiles_by_class[n])
        if len(rows) < 4:
            out["reason"] = f"too few profiles for class '{n}' ({len(rows)}, need 4)"
            return out
        mid = len(rows) // 2
        halves[n] = (rows[:mid], rows[mid:])
    if not all(n in halves for n in SIT_STAND):
        out["reason"] = "sitting and standing profiles are required"
        return out
    every = {n: [0, 0] for n in names}
    pair = {n: [0, 0] for n in SIT_STAND}
    for train_i, test_i in ((0, 1), (1, 0)):
        model = fit_posture_model({n: h[train_i] for n, h in halves.items()}, k=k, std_floor=std_floor)
        for n, h in halves.items():
            for block in block_average(h[test_i], block_n):
                label, _ = classify_profile(model, block)
                every[n][0] += 1
                every[n][1] += int(label == n)
                if n in pair:
                    label2, _ = classify_profile(model, block, SIT_STAND)
                    pair[n][0] += 1
                    pair[n][1] += int(label2 == n)
    allc = _tally(every)
    out.update(available=True, per_class=allc["per_class"], overall_accuracy=allc["accuracy"],
               blocks=allc["blocks"], chance_accuracy=round(1.0 / len(names), 4),
               sit_stand={**_tally(pair), "chance_accuracy": 0.5})
    return out


def quality_warnings(model: dict) -> list:
    """Warnings when sitting and standing are hard to tell apart."""
    out = []
    best = model.get("best_fisher")
    sc = model.get("self_check") or {}
    acc = (sc.get("sit_stand") or {}).get("accuracy") if sc.get("available") else None
    reasons = []
    if acc is not None and acc < MIN_SELF_CHECK_ACCURACY:
        reasons.append(f"sitting-vs-standing self-check {acc:.0%} (below {MIN_SELF_CHECK_ACCURACY:.0%}; "
                       "within-calibration, optimistic)")
    if best is None or best < MIN_FISHER:
        reasons.append(f"best subcarrier Fisher score {best if best is not None else 0:.2f} (below {MIN_FISHER:g})")
    if reasons:
        out.append(f"{SIMILAR_WARNING} ({'; '.join(reasons)})")
    if sc and not sc.get("available"):
        out.append(f"posture self-check unavailable: {sc.get('reason')}")
    return out

      :data:`MOVING_CONFIRM_S` when the current state is a still posture)
    * no posture model -> ``unknown`` with reason ``not calibrated``; the
      classifier never guesses sitting / standing without a model
    * layout differs from the model -> ``unknown``
    * otherwise the still frames of the last ``posture_window_s`` are averaged
      and classified (:func:`classify_profile`); ``empty`` maps to ``away``.
      A new still posture replaces the state only after it was the most likely
      class with probability >= ``min_confidence`` for ``hold_s``, or
      ``transition_confirm_s`` when a movement burst ended within
      :data:`RECENT_MOVEMENT_S` (sitting down / standing up).

    ``config`` is read on every frame (a :class:`backend.config.PostureConfig`),
    so settings changes apply immediately. Not thread-safe.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: PostureConfig) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.state = "unknown"
        self.state_since: Optional[float] = None
        self.last: Optional[PostureReading] = None
        self._window: deque = deque()
        self._cand: Optional[str] = None
        self._cand_since: Optional[float] = None
        self._cand_fast = False
        self._last_moving: Optional[float] = None
        self._moving_since: Optional[float] = None
        self._model_ref = None

    def _set(self, state: str, ts: float) -> None:
        if state != self.state:
            self.state = state
            self.state_since = ts
        elif self.state_since is None:
            self.state_since = ts

    def _clear_window(self) -> None:
        self._window.clear()
        self._cand = None
        self._cand_since = None

    def update(self, frame, profile, layout, model: Optional[dict], movement_threshold: float) -> PostureReading:
        cfg = self.config
        ts = float(frame.ts)
        motion = frame.motion_score
        if model is not self._model_ref:
            self._model_ref = model
            self._clear_window()
            if self.state in CLASS_STATES.values():
                self._set("unknown", ts)
        raw, probs, conf = None, {}, None
        if not frame.quality_ok or motion is None:
            reasons = list(getattr(frame, "quality_reasons", None) or [])
            reason = ("insufficient data quality: " + reasons[0]) if reasons else "no motion score yet"
            self._clear_window()
            self._moving_since = None
            self._set("unknown", ts)
        elif motion >= movement_threshold:
            raw = "moving"
            reason = f"motion score {motion:.2f} >= movement threshold {movement_threshold:.2f}"
            self._last_moving = ts
            self._clear_window()
            if self._moving_since is None:
                self._moving_since = ts
            if self.state not in CLASS_STATES.values() or ts - self._moving_since >= MOVING_CONFIRM_S:
                self._set("moving", ts)
        else:
            self._moving_since = None
            if model is None:
                reason = REASON_NOT_CALIBRATED
                self._clear_window()
                self._set("unknown", ts)
            elif layout is None or int(layout[1]) != int(model["n_subcarriers"]):
                reason = "the subcarrier layout does not match the calibration"
                self._clear_window()
                self._set("unknown", ts)
            elif profile is None or np.size(profile) != int(model["n_subcarriers"]):
                reason = "no amplitude profile"
                self._set("unknown", ts)
            else:
                raw, probs, conf, reason = self._classify(ts, profile, model)
        if (self.state == "moving" and raw != "moving" and self._last_moving is not None
                and ts - self._last_moving > cfg.hold_s + cfg.posture_window_s):
            self._set("unknown", ts)    # movement ended but no posture could be confirmed
        reading = PostureReading(ts=ts, raw_label=raw, state=self.state, probabilities=probs, confidence=conf,
                                 reason=reason, motion_score=motion, state_since=self.state_since)
        self.last = reading
        return reading

    def _classify(self, ts: float, profile, model: dict):
        cfg = self.config
        win = self._window
        win.append((ts, np.asarray(profile, dtype=float).copy()))
        while win and win[0][0] < ts - cfg.posture_window_s:
            win.popleft()
        if win[-1][0] - win[0][0] < cfg.posture_window_s * MIN_WINDOW_FILL:
            return None, {}, None, "collecting a posture window"
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            avg = np.nanmean(np.vstack([p for _, p in win]), axis=0)
        label, probs = classify_profile(model, avg)
        if label is None:
            self._cand = None
            return None, {}, None, "no usable subcarriers in the profile"
        conf = probs[label]
        raw = CLASS_STATES.get(label, label)
        probs = {CLASS_STATES.get(c, c): p for c, p in probs.items()}
        if conf < cfg.min_confidence:
            self._cand = None
            return raw, probs, conf, f"low confidence ({raw} p={conf:.2f} < {cfg.min_confidence:.2f})"
        if raw != self._cand:
            self._cand = raw
            self._cand_since = ts
            self._cand_fast = self._last_moving is not None and ts - self._last_moving <= RECENT_MOVEMENT_S
        need = cfg.transition_confirm_s if self._cand_fast else cfg.hold_s
        held = ts - self._cand_since
        if raw != self.state and held >= need:
            self._set(raw, ts)
        if raw == self.state:
            reason = f"posture model: {raw} (p={conf:.2f})"
        else:
            reason = f"posture model: {raw} (p={conf:.2f}), confirming {held:.1f}/{need:g} s"
        return raw, probs, conf, reason

"""Application configuration: dataclasses with tolerant JSON load/save.

The file lives at ``data/config.json`` and is created with defaults on first
use. Unknown keys are ignored and missing keys fall back to their defaults, so
older or hand-edited files keep working. Standard library only (the optional
ML tooling imports this module too).

import json
import os
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field, fields
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Optional

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DATA_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "data"
DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = DATA_DIR / "config.json"


@dataclass
class ProcessingConfig:
    """Signal processing parameters (see :mod:`backend.processing`)."""

    #: Sliding analysis window, seconds of host time.
    window_s: float = 1.0
    #: Hampel filter history length (packets) and threshold (scaled MADs).
    hampel_window: int = 7
    hampel_k: float = 3.0
    #: EMA smoothing factor per packet (1.0 = no smoothing).
    ema_alpha: float = 0.3
    #: Time constant of the slow adaptive reference profile used when no
    #: calibration baseline is set.
    reference_tau_s: float = 30.0
    #: Frames (motion feature snapshots) emitted per second of packet time.
    frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0
    #: Data-quality gates: below these a frame is flagged insufficient.
    min_packet_rate_hz: float = 20.0
    min_window_fill: float = 0.7
    stale_after_s: float = 1.0
    #: Noise references used to normalise the motion score while uncalibrated.
    #: Calibration (Milestone 3) replaces them with measured empty-room values.
    uncalibrated_variance_ref: float = 0.03
    uncalibrated_diff_ref: float = 0.01


@dataclass
class MotionThresholds:
    """Motion score thresholds. Calibrated empty room scores about 1.0.

    * score < ``movement``          -> empty room / low activity
    * ``movement`` <= score < ``rapid`` -> movement detected
    * score >= ``rapid``            -> rapid movement
    * ``low`` marks "still" (used later for post-event stillness checks)

    The defaults are uncalibrated guesses, not measured values.
    """

    low: float = 1.5
    movement: float = 2.5
    rapid: float = 6.0
    calibrated: bool = False


@dataclass
class FallConfig:
    """Explainable potential-fall heuristic (see :mod:`backend.detector`).

    A potential fall needs (1) a sudden motion spike, (2) post-event stillness
    that starts soon after the spike and lasts long enough, and (3) sufficient
    data quality over the whole evaluation window. Stillness alone is never a
    fall. Values of 0 for the two score thresholds mean "derive from the
    active motion thresholds" (calibrated when a calibration is loaded).
    """

    enabled: bool = True
    #: Spike: peak motion score must reach this (0 = use MotionThresholds.rapid).
    spike_threshold: float = 0.0
    #: Spike: the score must rise by at least ``min_rise_fraction * spike_threshold``
    #: within ``rise_window_s`` (a *sudden* increase, not sustained activity).
    rise_window_s: float = 1.5
    min_rise_fraction: float = 0.5
    #: Stillness: motion score at or below this (0 = use MotionThresholds.low) ...
    stillness_threshold: float = 0.0
    #: ... continuously for at least this long ...
    stillness_duration_s: float = 3.0
    #: ... starting no later than this after the last spike frame.
    max_gap_s: float = 2.0
    #: Quality: every frame in the evaluation window must be quality-ok and at
    #: least this packet rate.
    min_packet_rate_hz: float = 20.0
    #: After a detection, ignore new spikes for this long (seconds of data time).
    refractory_s: float = 30.0


@dataclass
class AlertConfig:
    """Alert handling (see :mod:`backend.alerts`)."""

    #: Countdown before the *simulated* caregiver notification.
    countdown_s: float = 30.0
    #: Events kept in memory for the dashboard (the JSONL file is append-only).
    event_log_max: int = 500
    #: An activity change is logged only after the new state held this long.
    activity_min_s: float = 1.0


@dataclass
class PostureConfig:
    """Sitting / standing tracking (see :mod:`backend.posture` and :mod:`backend.sitting`).

    Upright time = standing + moving (like Apple Watch stand hours, moving
    counts as standing). Valid ranges are in :data:`POSTURE_RANGES`.
    """

    #: Seconds of smoothed amplitude profiles averaged before classifying.
    posture_window_s: float = 3.0
    #: A still posture must have at least this probability ...
    min_confidence: float = 0.6
    #: ... for this long before the state changes ...
    hold_s: float = 5.0
    #: ... or this long when a movement burst ended within the last 5 s
    #: (sitting down / standing up produce one).
    transition_confirm_s: float = 2.0
    #: Unknown / no-data gaps shorter than this do not break a sitting streak.
    unknown_grace_s: float = 10.0
    #: Being away (empty room) longer than this ends a sitting streak.
    away_end_streak_s: float = 120.0
    #: Stand reminder once a sitting streak reaches this many minutes.
    reminder_after_min: float = 30.0
    #: Continuous upright time that counts as a stand break (ends the streak,
    #: clears the reminder).
    stand_break_s: float = 60.0
    #: Daily goal of stand hours.
    stand_goal_hours: int = 12
    #: An hour counts as a stand hour with at least this much upright time.
    stand_hour_min_s: float = 60.0


#: PostureConfig field -> (min, max), inclusive. Out-of-range values in the
#: config file are clamped; the API rejects them.
POSTURE_RANGES = {
    "posture_window_s": (1.0, 10.0),
    "min_confidence": (0.5, 0.99),
    "hold_s": (1.0, 60.0),
    "transition_confirm_s": (0.5, 30.0),
    "unknown_grace_s": (0.0, 300.0),
    "away_end_streak_s": (10.0, 3600.0),
    "reminder_after_min": (1.0, 180.0),
    "stand_break_s": (10.0, 600.0),
    "stand_goal_hours": (1, 24),
    "stand_hour_min_s": (10.0, 1800.0),
}


def _clamp_posture(cfg: PostureConfig) -> PostureConfig:
    for name, (lo, hi) in POSTURE_RANGES.items():
        v = getattr(cfg, name)
        if v != v:   # NaN
            v = getattr(PostureConfig(), name)
        setattr(cfg, name, type(lo)(min(hi, max(lo, v))))
    return cfg


@dataclass
class AppConfig:
    processing: ProcessingConfig = field(default_factory=ProcessingConfig)
    thresholds: MotionThresholds = field(default_factory=MotionThresholds)
    fall: FallConfig = field(default_factory=FallConfig)
    alerts: AlertConfig = field(default_factory=AlertConfig)
    posture: PostureConfig = field(default_factory=PostureConfig)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: Optional[dict]) -> "AppConfig":
        data = data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
        return cls(
            processing=_build(ProcessingConfig, data.get("processing")),
            thresholds=_build(MotionThresholds, data.get("thresholds")),
            fall=_build(FallConfig, data.get("fall")),
            alerts=_build(AlertConfig, data.get("alerts")),
            posture=_clamp_posture(_build(PostureConfig, data.get("posture"))),
        )

    def save(self, path=DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH) -> Path:
        path = Path(path)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        os.replace(tmp, path)
        return path

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path=DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH) -> "AppConfig":
        """Load ``path``; raises ``FileNotFoundError`` / ``ValueError`` on problems."""
        text = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: invalid JSON ({e})") from None
        return cls.from_dict(data)

    @classmethod
    def load_or_create(cls, path=DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH) -> "AppConfig":
        """Load ``path``, creating it with defaults if it does not exist."""
        path = Path(path)
        if not path.exists():
            cfg = cls()
            cfg.save(path)
            return cfg
        return cls.load(path)


def _build(dc_type, data: Any):
    """Instantiate ``dc_type`` from a dict, ignoring unknown keys and keeping
    defaults for missing or wrongly typed values."""
    obj = dc_type()
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return obj
    for f in fields(dc_type):
        if f.name not in data:
            continue
        default = getattr(obj, f.name)
        value = data[f.name]
        try:
            if isinstance(default, bool):
                if isinstance(value, bool):
                    setattr(obj, f.name, value)
            elif isinstance(default, int):
                setattr(obj, f.name, int(value))
            elif isinstance(default, float):
                setattr(obj, f.name, float(value))
            else:
                setattr(obj, f.name, value)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return obj

# EchoGuard firmware

Two standalone ESP-IDF projects derived from the official
[espressif/esp-csi get-started examples](https://github.com/espressif/esp-csi/tree/master/examples/get-started)
(`csi_send` and `csi_recv`):

| Project | Role | Based on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transmitter/` | ESP-NOW broadcast from fixed MAC `1a:00:00:00:00:00`, channel 11, HT40, MCS0 LGI, 100 Hz | `csi_send` |
| `receiver/` | STA + promiscuous, CSI enabled, filters the TX MAC, prints official `CSI_DATA` lines over serial | `csi_recv` |

No router, no mesh, no internet at runtime. The only network access needed is
on the **first receiver build**: the IDF component manager downloads
`esp_csi_gain_ctrl` (>=0.1.4) into `receiver/managed_components/`.

> Not verified here: these projects were written against the official examples
> but were **not compiled** on the development machine (ESP-IDF was not
> installed) and have not been run on hardware yet.

## Configuration (idf.py menuconfig)

| Option | Project | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ECHOGUARD_TX_CHANNEL` | transmitter | 11 | Wi-Fi channel 1..13 |
| `ECHOGUARD_TX_RATE_HZ` | transmitter | 100 | packets per second 10..200 |
| `ECHOGUARD_RX_CHANNEL` | receiver | 11 | must equal the TX channel |
| `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY` | receiver (classic chips) | y | print only the 128 LLTF values so 100 Hz fits 921600 baud |
| `ECHOGUARD_RX_MAX_CSI_BYTES` | receiver | 384 (612 on C5/C6) | per-packet copy size |
| `ECHOGUARD_RX_QUEUE_LEN` | receiver | 32 | callback-to-printer queue depth |

## Build and flash

Activate ESP-IDF first (`. $HOME/esp/esp-idf/export.sh`). Replace the port
with the one shown by `make ports`. Identify the chip first with the read-only
`esptool.py --port <PORT> chip_id` and pick the matching target.

Standard boards with a USB-UART bridge (CP210x / CH34x), console on UART:

```bash
# Receiver (pick ONE target: esp32 | esp32s3 | esp32c3 | esp32c6)
cd firmware/receiver
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX flash monitor

# Transmitter
cd firmware/transmitter
idf.py set-target esp32
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY flash monitor
```
